ann_79.text: Through this part, more daytime minutes (112 to 249) slightly raise the predicted chance of leaving, but only if the customer has no voice-mail plan: from about 2% to about 4%, against below 1% either way with a plan.

For customers without a voice-mail plan, daytime minutes slightly add to it only once they rise above about 218 minutes, from about 2% to about 7% for the typical customer (on the training data only).

This part acts on 1033 of 4000 customers, 283 of whom left; for the typical one (in Alabama, with about 234 daytime minutes and no voice-mail plan) it slightly raises the chance from about 2% to about 6% (on the training data only).
For that customer, a voice-mail plan slightly lowers it from about 6% to about 2%.
Across the usual range, more daytime minutes and a higher daytime charge slightly raise it to about 3% to 4% (on the training data only).

ann_80.text: Through this part, the daytime charge clearly adds to the predicted chance of leaving only once it rises above about 41.59 US dollars: for the typical customer, going from 0 to 46.09 US dollars moves it from about 2% to about 8%.
A higher evening charge (11.76 to 22.57 US dollars) slightly raises it, but only if the daytime charge is above 30.69 US dollars: from about 2% to about 5%, against about 2% either way otherwise.
Across the usual range, a higher daytime charge and a higher evening charge slightly raise it, to about 2% to 3%.
Voice-mail messages slightly raise it only while they stay below about 20 messages, from about 2% to about 4% for the typical customer (on the training data only).

More international minutes (7 to 14) slightly lower it from about 3% to about 2%, for a typical customer in Virginia they slightly lower it once they rise above about 3 minutes (from about 4% to about 2%), and being in Alabama slightly lowers it (on the training data only).

ann_81.text: Through this part, customer-service calls clearly add to the predicted chance of leaving from 3 calls upwards: for a typical such customer, going from 0 to 4 calls moves it from about 2% to about 13%.

For the typical customer this part acts on (one with 3 customer-service calls and about 166 daytime minutes), a higher daytime charge (19.07 to 42.40 US dollars) clearly lowers it from about 11% to about 2%.

Customer-service calls slightly raise it, and even more so if the daytime charge is 30.69 US dollars or less: going from 0 to 3 calls moves it from about 2% to about 6%, against about 2% either way above that charge.
This part acts on 1303 of 4000 customers, 302 of whom left; for the typical one it slightly raises the chance from about 2% to about 3%.
An international plan slightly raises it and being in South Dakota slightly lowers it through this part (on the training data only).

ann_82.text: Through this part, being in Utah, Iowa or Arkansas slightly raises the predicted chance of leaving to about 2% to 3%, and North Dakota and New Mexico slightly lower it, staying at about 2% (on the training data only).
More voice-mail messages slightly raise it, staying at about 2% (on the training data only).

ann_83.text: Across the whole model, an international plan clearly raises the typical customer's predicted chance of leaving from about 2% to about 24%.

More voice-mail messages (0 to 32) raise it to about 10%, and California and Washington, compared with the states the model does not single out, raise it to about 9% and 7% (on the training data only).

New Jersey and Texas slightly raise it to about 4% to 5% and New York, Utah, Minnesota, Ohio, Oregon, Arizona, Indiana, Iowa and Arkansas to about 2% to 3%, while Vermont slightly lowers it to below 1% and Alaska, Wyoming, Illinois, Wisconsin, Nebraska, Missouri, North Dakota, Alabama, New Mexico and South Dakota to about 1% to 2% (on the training data only).
A voice-mail plan slightly lowers it to below 1%, while three customer-service calls rather than none and a higher evening charge slightly raise it, to about 2% to 3%.

More daytime minutes (112 to 249), more international and evening minutes, a higher night-time charge and a longer account slightly raise it to about 3% to 4%, while an area code other than 415 and more evening calls slightly lower it, staying at about 2% (on the training data only).
It ignores daytime calls, international calls, international charge, night-time calls and night-time minutes.

ann_79.original: HYPOTHESIS: two ReLU hinges on daytime usage that raise churn for heavy day users, mainly those without a voice-mail plan. total_day_minutes and total_day_charge are identical after z-scoring (max diff 5e-4), so the leaf uses both interchangeably. 1254 = relu(0.42*day - 0.73): on for day z > 1.74 (164 rows, churn 62% vs 12%), logit +2.08 per unit (up to +1.26). 3460 = relu(0.86*day - 0.83*voice_mail_plan - 0.85): on for day z > 0.39 without a voice-mail plan, z > 2.5 with one (995 rows, churn 28% vs 9.5%), logit +2.25 per unit (up to +5.3). EVIDENCE (train, n=4000): closed form above (max err 0.002); sensitivity: 3460 driven by voice_mail_plan (0.21) and day (0.21 total). Combined usage logit (with totalChargeChain): no voice-mail plan, day z>1 and eve z>1 -> +5.2 logit, empirical churn 94%; same usage with a voice-mail plan -> churn 10%. Replacing this leaf by its best linear fit costs 0.008 train AUC; mean-ablating 3460 costs 0.016.
ann_79.proposed: Heavy daytime usage slightly raises the chance of leaving, only for customers without a voice-mail plan, starting at about 218 minutes.

ann_80.original: HYPOTHESIS: a hinge chain on the combined day+evening bill. 5604 = relu(1.14*day_charge + 1.26*eve_charge - 0.94) (eve_charge == eve_minutes after z-scoring) is on for 1143 rows (churn 26%); 4045 = relu(0.60*day_charge + 0.73*5604 - 1.02) sharpens it (626 rows, churn 41% vs 9%), logit +1.57 per unit (up to +7.0). 9871 = relu(0.49*5604 - 0.84) is a higher threshold (244 rows, churn 56%) with a small negative logit weight (-0.24) and a tiny relay path. 387 = relu(0.94 - 1.07*vmail_messages + 0.56*intl_minutes + 0.04*state:1 - 0.86*4045) is on for 76% of rows; its -0.36 output weight lowers churn for customers with few voice-mail messages and many international minutes, and a high bill switches it off (removing that negative term). EVIDENCE: closed form (max err 0.008), sensitivity (4045: eve 0.14, day 0.22; 387: vmail messages 0.81, intl minutes 0.42). Linearising the leaf costs 0.008 AUC; jointly with dayUsageHinges 0.025 (the two overlap: both are day-usage hinges).
ann_80.proposed: The combined bill: the daytime charge adds to the chance of leaving above about 41.59 US dollars (about 2% to 8%), and the evening charge adds slightly only when the daytime charge is above 30.69 US dollars; voice-mail and international-minute effects here are slight.

ann_81.original: HYPOTHESIS: customer-service-call hinges, with an interaction against day usage: many calls by low-usage customers = churn. 9203 = relu(0.66*cs - 0.67) is on at >=3 calls (848 rows, churn 25%), logit +1.41 per unit. 5395 = relu(0.71*cs - 0.65*day_charge - 0.75) is on at >=4 calls unless day z > ~0.9, or 3 calls with below-average day usage (810 rows), logit +1.93 per unit (up to +6.0). 553 = relu(0.51*cs + 0.28*international_plan - 0.68*state:41 - 0.66): >=1 call with an international plan or >=4 without (555 rows, churn 46%); reaches the logit only via the always-on relay (+0.14 per unit, max +0.45); state:41 rows switch it off (66 rows, effect <= 0.15 logit). EVIDENCE (train): table of this leaf's logit contribution / empirical churn by calls x day z-bin: 4 calls & day z<-1: +3.8 / 95%; 4 calls & day z>1: +0.8 / 33%; 5 calls & day z<-1: +5.6 / 100%; <=2 calls: ~0 / 5-9% (except the high-usage bin, handled by the usage leaves). number_customer_service_calls has no direct edge to the output, so this leaf is its only route: mean-ablating the leaf costs 0.113 train AUC; replacing it by its best linear fit costs 0.021, the largest nonlinear gain of any part.
ann_81.proposed: Customer-service calls add to the chance of leaving from 3 calls upwards (about 2% to 13% at 4 calls), and more so for customers with a low daytime charge; for the customers it acts on, a higher daytime charge lowers it (about 11% to 2%).

ann_82.original: HYPOTHESIS (revised): rare-state units that are almost inert. 14 hidden nodes driven only by state one-hots (states 50, 23, 22, 1, 28, 32, 44, 12, 2; ~55-105 rows each, large z-values) plus a tiny vmail-messages term. The cascade 3854->13212->8290->948->{13939,11368}->14533->1887 is on for <=105 rows and reaches the output through weights -0.09 then -0.015: zero measurable effect. 1887 (state:28) moves the logit by at most -0.23; 7740 (state:44, always on via bias) by at most +0.40 on state:44 rows; 4332 (state:12) +0.07; 15985 (state:2) +0.02; 3854 (state:32/44) feeds the relay with activation <=0.08. EVIDENCE: closed form (max err 0.022, sympy rounding through the deep cascade); sensitivities all <0.04 except 7740/state:44 (0.98 per unit of activation but output weight 0.05). Mean-ablating the whole leaf changes train AUC by -0.0002; its best linear fit has R2 1.000. The large per-state effects in this network are in the root's direct linear edges, not here.
ann_82.proposed: Rare-state adjustments for Utah, Iowa, Arkansas, North Dakota and New Mexico, plus voice-mail messages; all effects are slight and seen on the training data only.

ann_83.original: HYPOTHESIS: churn logit = -2.00 + linear term (direct edges) + dayUsageHinges + totalChargeChain + serviceCallsHinges + rareStateUnits + an always-on affine relay; output = sigmoid. Additive (parallel) composition at the output, plus a serial path: 553 (serviceCalls), 9871 (charge) and 3854 (states) feed the relay 12977/2377 -> 5868 -> 7162 -> output, which is active on all 4000 training rows and so contributes a constant (about -1.28) plus small linear terms. Linear term: international_plan +0.77/SD (+2.67 logit for plan holders), voice_mail_plan -0.86/SD (-2.37 for holders), vmail messages +0.41, intl minutes +0.45, eve minutes +0.22, night charge +0.22, account_length +0.12, and 17 per-state offsets (largest: state:46 -1.89, state:4 +1.48, state:47 +1.22, state:31 +0.86, state:0 -0.82, state:50 -0.76 logit on their 41-90 rows). 33 inputs are unconnected (zero effect). EVIDENCE (train, local mean-ablation and linearisation): full AUC 0.910; all hidden parts mean-ablated (direct edges only) 0.717; all hidden parts replaced by their best joint linear fit 0.835 (cf. parts.original_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: churn logit = -2.00 + linear term (direct edges) + dayUsageHinges + totalChargeChain + serviceCallsHinges + rareStateUnits + an always-on affine relay; output = sigmoid. Additive (parallel) composition at the output, plus a serial path: 553 (serviceCalls), 9871 (charge) and 3854 (states) feed the relay 12977/2377 -> 5868 -> 7162 -> output, which is active on all 4000 training rows and so contributes a constant (about -1.28) plus small linear terms. Linear term: international_plan +0.77/SD (+2.67 logit for plan holders), voice_mail_plan -0.86/SD (-2.37 for holders), vmail messages +0.41, intl minutes +0.45, eve minutes +0.22, night charge +0.22, account_length +0.12, and 17 per-state offsets (largest: state:46 -1.89, state:4 +1.48, state:47 +1.22, state:31 +0.86, state:0 -0.82, state:50 -0.76 logit on their 41-90 rows). 33 inputs are unconnected (zero effect). L2 logistic regression train 0.843). parts.name: serviceCallsHinges
parts.original_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: customer-service-call hinges, with an interaction against day usage: many calls by low-usage customers = churn. 9203 = relu(0.66*cs - 0.67) is on at >=3 calls (848 rows, churn 25%), logit +1.41 per unit. 5395 = relu(0.71*cs - 0.65*day_charge - 0.75) is on at >=4 calls unless day z > ~0.9, or 3 calls with below-average day usage (810 rows), logit +1.93 per unit (up to +6.0). 553 = relu(0.51*cs + 0.28*international_plan - 0.68*state:41 - 0.66): >=1 call with an international plan or >=4 without (555 rows, churn 46%); reaches the logit only via the always-on relay (+0.14 per unit, max +0.45); state:41 rows switch it off (66 rows, effect <= 0.15 logit). EVIDENCE (train): table of this leaf's logit contribution / empirical churn by calls x day z-bin: 4 calls & day z<-1: +3.8 / 95%; 4 calls & day z>1: +0.8 / 33%; 5 calls & day z<-1: +5.6 / 100%; <=2 calls: ~0 / 5-9% (except the high-usage bin, handled by the usage leaves). number_customer_service_calls has no direct edge to the output, so this leaf is its only route: mean-ablating the leaf costs 0.113 train AUC; replacing it by its best linear fit costs 0.021, the largest nonlinear gain of any part.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: dayUsageHinges
parts.original_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: two ReLU hinges on daytime usage that raise churn for heavy day users, mainly those without a voice-mail plan. total_day_minutes and total_day_charge are identical after z-scoring (max diff 5e-4), so the leaf uses both interchangeably. 1254 = relu(0.42*day - 0.73): on for day z > 1.74 (164 rows, churn 62% vs 12%), logit +2.08 per unit (up to +1.26). 3460 = relu(0.86*day - 0.83*voice_mail_plan - 0.85): on for day z > 0.39 without a voice-mail plan, z > 2.5 with one (995 rows, churn 28% vs 9.5%), logit +2.25 per unit (up to +5.3). EVIDENCE (train, n=4000): closed form above (max err 0.002); sensitivity: 3460 driven by voice_mail_plan (0.21) and day (0.21 total). Combined usage logit (with totalChargeChain): no voice-mail plan, day z>1 and eve z>1 -> +5.2 logit, empirical churn 94%; same usage with a voice-mail plan -> churn 10%. Replacing this leaf by its best linear fit costs 0.008 train AUC; mean-ablating 3460 costs 0.016.

parts.name: totalChargeChain
parts.original_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a hinge chain on the combined day+evening bill. 5604 = relu(1.14*day_charge + 1.26*eve_charge - 0.94) (eve_charge == eve_minutes after z-scoring) is on for 1143 rows (churn 26%); 4045 = relu(0.60*day_charge + 0.73*5604 - 1.02) sharpens it (626 rows, churn 41% vs 9%), logit +1.57 per unit (up to +7.0). 9871 = relu(0.49*5604 - 0.84) is a higher threshold (244 rows, churn 56%) with a small negative logit weight (-0.24) and a tiny relay path. 387 = relu(0.94 - 1.07*vmail_messages + 0.56*intl_minutes + 0.04*state:1 - 0.86*4045) is on for 76% of rows; its -0.36 output weight lowers churn for customers with few voice-mail messages and many international minutes, and a high bill switches it off (removing that negative term). EVIDENCE: closed form (max err 0.008), sensitivity (4045: eve 0.14, day 0.22; 387: vmail messages 0.81, intl minutes 0.42). Linearising the leaf costs 0.008 AUC; jointly with dayUsageHinges 0.025 (the two overlap: both are day-usage hinges).

parts.name: rareStateUnits
parts.original_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS (revised): rare-state units that are almost inert. 14 hidden nodes driven only by state one-hots (states 50, 23, 22, 1, 28, 32, 44, 12, 2; ~55-105 rows each, large z-values) plus a tiny vmail-messages term. The cascade 3854->13212->8290->948->{13939,11368}->14533->1887 is on for <=105 rows and reaches the output through weights -0.09 then -0.015: zero measurable effect. 1887 (state:28) moves the logit by at most -0.23; 7740 (state:44, always on via bias) by at most +0.40 on state:44 rows; 4332 (state:12) +0.07; 15985 (state:2) +0.02; 3854 (state:32/44) feeds the relay with activation <=0.08.
